title: Realtime chat sandbox onramp and resilience play
summary: Intro demo of Redwood hosted chat API focused on streaming behavior, commons params (temperature, max_tokens, stop), and retry/backoff patterns. Quick run through of Console sandbox, a simple streaming integration example, and discussion of enterprise concerns (VPC, audit logs, SOC2). Agreed to run a 2-week sandbox POC and exchange security questionnaire.
topics: Next steps: sandbox POC and security docs
next_steps: Redwood: send sandbox invite + sample integration snippets (Maya)
Customer: share internal perf target and sample prompt set (Priya)
Redwood: provide SOC2 summary and KMS integration notes (Leo)
action_items: Maya - send sandbox creds and quickstart link by 2025-10-17
Priya - share 20 sample prompts and latency SLO by 2025-10-20
Leo - attach SOC2 snapshot and KMS notes into deal thread by 2025-10-18
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're on pacific time here, quick intro, i'm maya, AE at Redwood. Leo and Sam from the eng team are here as well. before we start, any scheduling constraints?
[00:18] Carlos Mendes: no, we have about 45 minutes, perfect. thanks maya.
[00:35] Maya Chen: cool, the plan — quick console tour, then a short live sandbox run (streaming), and we'll talk about retries and security. we'll leave time for q's.
[00:50] Priya Nair: sounds great, we're primarily evaluating hosted first, we may move to dedicated later if perf/cost needs it.
[01:05] Leo Park: quick note — when we say hosted, you get the hosted api with streaming and console sandbox. latency varies by model and region; we'll show controls.
[01:22] Ava Li: can you show how we handle partial responses and reconnection? that's a big one for our chat flows.
[01:35] Sam Ortiz: yea, good question. we'll demo streaming chunking, and the client-side retry pattern — idempotency tokens + resume behavior. caveat: resumable KV cache isn't automatic on reconnect, you typically rehydrate conversation state from client cache.
[01:58] Speaker 1: uh is that like kafka?
[02:04] Maya Chen: not kafka, just client state. okay jumping into console — (screen share) — here's the sandbox tab. you can spin up a session with one click. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/sandbox (note: shortened link in recording).
[02:28] [screen noise / typing]
[02:40] Leo Park: demo note: streaming data comes as delta tokens, we flush every ~100ms server-side but chunk sizes change based on tokenization. that affects perceived latency.
[02:58] Priya Nair: sometimes tokens arrive in weird splits, we saw that with another provider where a token got split mid-word. how consistent is that?
[03:10] Leo Park: it's model-tokenizer dependent, you may see line breaks or fragmented words. client should handle joins. we have post-processing hints in the SDK; i'll send the snippet.
[03:28] Maya Chen: quick live example — we'll run a simple conversation prompt, stream enabled.
[03:38] [00:03 pause - typing]
[03:45] Transcriptor (auto): "Starting stream..."
[03:50] RedwoodBot: hi there, how can i help today?
[04:02] Priya Nair: okay that's the basic stream. what's the param set you'd recommend for a chat widget with low latency?
[04:12] Leo Park: for low-latency short replies: temperature 0.0-0.4, max_tokens 60-120, top_p 0.9; also use streaming and smaller token budgets. use prefix caching for repeated prompts to cut cost.
[04:35] Ava Li: prefix caching — does that store user data? how long is it retained?
[04:42] Sam Ortiz: good Q — caching can be ephemeral by session and not logged if you disable analytics. for hosted we default to no long-term retention unless you opt-in. this is configurable via retention flags.
[04:58] Carlos Mendes: we need KMS integration — keys must be under our control.
[05:05] Leo Park: we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; for hosted we offer envelope encryption with optional KMS linkups. i'll share the diagram and different modes.
[05:22] [small crosstalk]
[05:30] Priya Nair: can you walk through retry patterns? we saw 500s under load last sprint with our current provider.
[05:40] Maya Chen: absolutely. pattern we recommend: client uses a short timeout for streaming, on disconnect retry with exponential backoff and same idempotency token, but the server-side handling matters — if partial output was committed, you should fetch the last event id and resume or ask the model to continue.
[06:05] Leo Park: also consider a fallback model variant (cheaper or smaller) — Redwood routing can fail over to a compatible variant automatically based on policy. you'll configure that in the console under Deployments -> Fallbacks.
[06:25] Priya Nair: fallback automatic — is that per-organization or per-route?
[06:30] Sam Ortiz: per-route, you can pin on a route-level policy.
[06:36] Ava Li: i saw something about tokens and streaming windows — any tips to avoid double-charges if we retry?
[06:44] Leo Park: use idempotency and short session caching; charges are per token accepted by the runtime — if you send duplicate requests you'll pay twice unless the server recognizes the idempotency token and returns cached result. we have a 60s idempotency window by default.
[07:00] Carlos Mendes: so for long polls we should chunk into smaller messages?
[07:06] Leo Park: yes, or use streaming with partials — smaller chunks keep perceived latency low and make retries cheaper.
[07:14] [10:00 minutes mark: rough timekeeping noted]
[07:22] Maya Chen: showing param panel — you can change temp, top_p, frequency penalties live, and run A/B of two model variants.
[07:35] Priya Nair: can we programmatically toggle cache and quantization profiles?
[07:42] Sam Ortiz: quantization profiles are a serving-level thing, not runtime-toggleable in hosted unless you choose a specific model flavor. Console Optimize will recommend profiles based on workload.
[07:58] Priya Nair: what about long-term history? we need 90-day retention for logs for compliance.
[08:05] Leo Park: enterprise plans include audit log retention options. hosted has add-on for extended retention and SIEM forwarding. we'll attach the pricing appendix.
[08:20] Ava Li: ok let's do a quick integration show — front-end calls small POST, opens eventsource for stream. what about reconnect idempotency sample?
[08:32] Sam Ortiz: here's the pseudo: create request with conv_id + idempotency; open SSE; on disconnect, retry with same idempotency token and resume cursor. i will paste the snippet in the notes.
[08:45] [typing, link pasted] Link: https://redwood.ai/dev/snippets/reconnect-example
[08:55] Michael O'Neal: any limits on concurrent streams per workspace?
[09:01] Leo Park: default quotas apply; enterprise can reserve dedicated capacity for higher concurrency. Dedicated pools give deterministic throughput.
[09:14] Carlos Mendes: cost ballpark for hosted chat?
[09:18] Maya Chen: we'll send a tailored cost model, but for short responses we often recommend the small footprint models and caching to lower token counts. examples included in the pricing sheet we'll attach.
[09:30] Priya Nair: is there an SDK for node mobile?
[09:35] Sam Ortiz: Node and Python SDKs, plus a lightweight JS client for browser SSE. mobile uses same client code path.
[09:44] [interruption — connection jitter for 10s]
[09:56] Priya Nair: sorry, lost you for a sec — you mentioned SSO?
[10:00] Maya Chen: yes, SSO via SAML/SCIM provisioning available on enterprise tiers.
[10:08] Ava Li: quick Q on safety filters — do you support red-teamed models or content filters?
[10:14] Leo Park: we have optional moderation hooks and content filters at request time; plus model-level safety tuning. we'll share the safety brief.
[10:26] Priya Nair: outstanding, could you also include the perf bench doc? we want to see p95 under concurrent connections.
[10:33] Maya Chen: yes, we'll run a small benchmark for your prompt set; that would be part of the sandbox POC.
[10:41] Carlos Mendes: timeline — we're aiming for an internal decision in 6 weeks.
[10:47] Maya Chen: perfect — two-week sandbox then a perf review, then proposal.
[10:54] [20:00 min mark — mid-call check]
[11:02] Sam Ortiz: i'll call out a tricky gotcha — when a stream fails mid-generation and client retries, if you don't use idempotency the second request creates a new generation which can produce overlapping content. our SDK tries to detect and dedupe by default but you should still use tokens.
[11:22] Priya Nair: how often do you see partial double-deliveries in practice?
[11:27] Leo Park: low, but spikes happen when upstream GPUs saturate — that's where dedicated helps.
[11:35] Michael O'Neal: competitor question — how is your SLAs vs LargeCloudX?
[11:40] Maya Chen: hosted has strong SLOs for availability and we publish latency percentiles per-region. Dedicated/reserved gives SLA-backed targets. we'll send the SLA doc.
[11:52] Ava Li: can you show the console trace view?
[11:58] [screen share — tracing UI]
[12:08] Sam Ortiz: here's the per-request trace, you can see token times, kernel times, and where a retry happened. it's useful for diagnosing hotspots.
[12:20] Priya Nair: that's gold, we'll want access to that.
[12:25] Maya Chen: note on data residency — hosted currently supports NA and EU regions; Private on-prem addresses other residency needs.
[12:38] Carlos Mendes: ok final recap?
[12:42] Maya Chen: recap: Redwood to send sandbox + quickstart + SOC2/KMS notes; run a 2-week trial with your 20 prompts; Redwood runs perf bench; customer to confirm latency SLOs and compliance items.
[12:58] Priya Nair: thanks, that works.
[13:05] Maya Chen: i'll follow up in the thread with links and due dates. thanks all.
[13:12] [call ends]
